The key file of your hospital lets the server recognise an encounter in later uploads, for example when a period is exported twice, without learning who the patient is. Only your hospital holds the key file; the server never sees it.
When should you change the key?

Check the links between ED visits and IVENA allocations: confirm or reject proposals, resolve conflicts and apply swaps.
Choose a hospital whose links you may review.
You may not review links for any hospital. The hospital owner can grant the encounter access "Review matches".
"Agreement" (0–1) compares the features of a pair with its competing candidates and the option "no match". It is a ranking set by judgement, not a probability that the link is correct.
Allocations count by expected IVENA arrival, visits by ED admission (or first assessment contact). At most {days} days.
Each allocation counts once; shares refer to all allocations in the period. Rejected pairs and swap proposals are counted separately.
ED visits in the period: {count, number}
Linked = automatic or confirmed link. Self-presenters usually have no allocation; an unlinked visit is not an error.
ED visits of the period without automatic or confirmed link. Most are self-presenters, for whom no allocation is expected. A visit with an open proposal leads to the review of its allocation.

No ED admission documented; the first contact of the initial assessment is used instead.
Linked automatically by the matcher (agreement {score}, pass {pass}). It is effective without confirmation.

All visits of the hospital from {before} minutes before to {after} minutes after the expected arrival with at most {age} years age difference. The agreement compares them with each other; the stored score of a pair comes from the matcher pass that found it.
